pcm.fact: DASA UG 2026 is open to Foreign Nationals, OCI, PIO and NRI candidates and admission is on JEE (Main) 2026 ranks (Paper 1 for B.E./B.Tech.).
DASA UG 2026 now runs together with CSAB Special Rounds via csab.nic.in (not a separate dasanit.org UG process); dasanit.org now shows only DASA PG 2026.
Candidates born on or after 1 October 2001 are eligible (DOB as in Class X certificate).
B.E./B.Tech. needs Mathematics, Physics and one of Chemistry/Biotechnology/Computer Science/Biology in Class XII with at least 75% (CGPA 7.5/10) aggregate in 5 subjects.
Candidates appearing in 2025-26 with results expected by 30 September 2026 may also apply.

Class XII or equivalent from any system recognised by AIU is accepted; Annexure 2 lists AIU-equivalent boards including IB Diploma, Gulf 12-year secondary certificates, GCE/IGCSE with A-levels, 12-year US High School Diploma from accredited schools (not online/distance), Abitur; unlisted boards must get an AIU equivalence certificate.

Indian nationals/OCI-PIO(I) need at least two years of education covering Class 11 and 12 (not beyond) in a foreign country during the last 8 years and must pass Class 12 from abroad; foreign nationals studying in any country including India are eligible.
DASA seats are supernumerary, up to 15% of each institute's seats programme-wise; 5% (one third of DASA seats) is reserved for CIWG.

Tags: DASA (SAARC) for SAARC foreign nationals/OCI/PIO; DASA (Non-SAARC) for other foreign nationals/OCI/PIO and also NRI; DASA-CIWG for NRIs with either or both parents working in UAE, Bahrain, Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar or Saudi Arabia.
Either parent must be working, or have worked, in a Gulf country on any date in 2026, with passport, visa, work permit and employer certificate (Annexure 12) as proof.
OCI/PIO card holders (card before 4 March 2021) are not eligible for DASA-CIWG seats; only NRIs with parents in the listed Gulf countries are.
Initial fee US$4300 (Non-SAARC, includes US$300 non-refundable registration and US$4000 first-semester tuition), US$2300 SAARC, US$300 plus INR 62500 for CIWG.
DASA gives no category/gender supernumerary benefit except CIWG; female supernumerary seats for NRI/OCI-PIO(I) exist only in CSAB Special Rounds.

OCI/PIO holders with card issued after 4 March 2021 are OCI/PIO(F) treated as foreign nationals; those with card before 4 March 2021 may choose OCI/PIO(F) or OCI/PIO(I) (at par with Indians); choice cannot be changed.
OCI/PIO(I) passing Class XII in India are at par with Indians for state code; those passing Class XII abroad get Other State or All India quota seats only, not Home State seats, in NIT+ system.

In JoSAA, non-Indian nationals and OCI/PIO(F) get a Foreign tag; they get supernumerary seats in IITs/IISc (up to 10% of seats, programme-wise, no reservation) and are not served by JoSAA/CSAB for NIT+ (they go via DASA).

NIT+ system needs Class XII with five subjects and at least 75% aggregate (65% SC/ST/PwD) or top 20 percentile of the board; Annexure 2(a) for IITs carries the same 75% rule; first appearance in 2024, 2025 or 2026.
For Indian nationals passing Class XII abroad, state code of eligibility comes from permanent address in the Indian passport.

Maharashtra 2026-27 brochure has separate candidature for NRI and for Foreign Student/OCI/PIO; OCI with status before 4 March 2021 can use Maharashtra or All India candidature if they passed 10th and 10+2 in India and lived in India 10+ years.

10+2 with Physics and Mathematics compulsory plus one of Chemistry/Biotechnology/Biology/Technical Vocational/Computer Science/IT/Informatics Practices/Agriculture/Engineering Graphics/Business Studies/Electronics/Entrepreneurship with at least 45% in these subjects together.
Supernumerary seats up to 15% of sanctioned intake: one third for children of Indian workers in Gulf countries, two thirds for OCI/PIO/Foreign Students; vacant seats may go to NRIs.
Institutional quota allows maximum 5% NRI seats if approved by the authority.
Merit list for NRI/OCI/PIO/Foreign/CIWG is on percentage in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics together at the qualifying exam, applied through a separate portal (not CAP).
From Ordinance VI of 2025 an NRI is a person 'not ordinary resident' under the Income Tax Act with an NRI certificate from an Indian Mission, including child or ward (circular is for 2025-26).
KEAM 2026: OCI (including PIO) holders are treated at par with Indian citizens for admission but get no reservation or fee concession; only Indian citizens otherwise.

Higher Secondary with Physics and Mathematics compulsory and Chemistry as optional with at least 45% marks put together (Computer Science, Biotechnology or Biology substituted if Chemistry not studied).
KEAM prospectus 5.7 defines NRI-quota eligibility (dependent on a relative working abroad) in the medical/dental context; an NRI quota for engineering seats is not stated in the clauses read.

NK II candidates (no Kerala residence/schooling link) can get engineering seats allotted by the CEE only after the second phase in Government Cost-Sharing colleges if Keralite/NK I are unavailable, and can use government and management quota seats in private self-financing engineering colleges; the prospectus also says NK II are not eligible for engineering in Government colleges.
TNEA 2026: OCI/PIO card holders who are natives of Tamil Nadu may take part in counselling in Open Category (from 2023-24), except OCI/PIO born abroad after 4 March 2021.
TNEA general category needs a pass in HSC (+1 and +2) with minimum average 45% in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry together (40% BC/MBC).

AP EAPCET 2026 lets Indian nationals and PIO/OCI card holders appear if they belong to Andhra Pradesh (local/non-local rules); 45% in subjects together (40% reserved); Maths, Physics, Chemistry; age 16 by 31 Dec 2026 for engineering.
Weightage of marks for PIO/OCI card holders is decided by a committee of the competent authority.

VIT page (2027-28 cycle): NRI means Indian national whose parent or real sibling lives and works abroad and sponsors; PCM aggregate 60% with at least 50% in Mathematics; Class 12 passed in 2025/2026 or appearing 2027; direct NRI application exists but NRI/OCI via general route take VITEEE.

VIT foreign nationals (valid foreign passport, OCI listed among eligible): Maths and Physics compulsory plus a third subject, 55% aggregate, Maths at least 50%; English medium needed; UK A-levels, IB, US High School, Canada Grade 12 accepted; UGC equivalence certificate for others.

BITS International Students Admission 2026-27 is only for foreign-passport holders: Physics, Maths and Chemistry/Biology/Biotech/Technical Vocational, 75% aggregate with 60% in each, plus SAT at least 1160 of 1600 taken after 1 Feb 2024; Class 12 first attempt in 2025 or 2026.

BITSAT is open to Indian and international students; the BITS first-degree rule is 75% aggregate in PCM with at least 60% in each subject (read in the BITSAT-2022 modality PDF; 2026-27 cycle shown as closed).

MEA: OCI under section 7A of the Citizenship Act 1955 covers foreign nationals who were or were eligible to be Indian citizens on or after 26 Jan 1950 (and children/grandchildren); citizens or descendants of Pakistan, Bangladesh or notified countries excluded.

pcb.fact: An OCI cardholder (including a PIO cardholder) is a foreign national holding a foreign passport and is not a citizen of India (MHA notification of 4 March 2021, quoted by NTA).
PIO cardholders with valid cards on 9 January 2015 are deemed OCI cardholders; OCI is registered under Section 7A of the Citizenship Act 1955 (read from a search result, page not fetched).
Following the Supreme Court judgment of 3 Feb 2023 (WP(C) 891/2021), an OCI is eligible for UG Medical/Dental/AYUSH courses subject to NEET and the rules of regulators and counselling authorities.

NTA's 2023 corrigendum said OCI/PIO are treated as foreigners, eligible for NRI seats only and not for Indian National Seats including paid seats of deemed universities; this is 2023 text, the 2026 bulletin could not be read.

KEAM 2026: only Indian citizens are eligible for professional courses unless notified; OCI (including PIO) cardholders are treated at par with Indian citizens for admission only, with no reservation or fee concession (SC order 3 Feb 2023, G.O.(Rt)1620/2023/HEdn).
KEAM 2026: only candidates who qualify in NEET-UG 2026 and meet the nativity conditions are considered for MBBS, BDS and AYUSH courses.
KEAM 2026 MBBS/BDS: pass in Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English individually, with minimum 50% in PCB taken together (Kerala Higher Secondary or recognised equivalent).
KEAM 2026 MBBS/BDS: PCB aggregate minimum is 40% for SC/ST, SEBC and PD-quota candidates instead of 50%.

KEAM 2026: an applicant who depends on father, mother, siblings (including first cousins), spouse, half sibling, adopted parent or a parent's sibling working abroad may apply under NRI quota (G.O.(MS)243/2014/H&FWD).

KEAM 2026 NRI quota: upload sponsor's passport copy and visa/Green Card/Norka Roots ID/OCI document showing the sponsor's job, visa valid on the application closing date, an Embassy-attested employer certificate if the job is not shown, and a Revenue-authority relationship certificate.
KEAM 2026 has an NRI sponsorship affidavit (Annexure XL) in which the sponsor undertakes to bear the candidate's whole tuition and other fees, non-refundable.
KEAM 2026: NRI seats in self-financing medical and dental colleges are filled through CEE common counselling (Supreme Court order of 9 May 2017).
KEAM 2026: unallotted NRI-Minority seats become NRI Open, and unallotted NRI Open seats become State Merit (G.O.(Rt)1517/2022/H&FWD).
KEAM 2026: if NRI seats would lapse for want of candidates with a domicile certificate, admission is made without it (Supreme Court 2020 judgment).
GGSIPU 2026-27 international brochure: 25% of seats may be filled supernumerary from Foreign Nationals, PIO and International Students under the PIHEAD programme; unfilled seats go to no one else.

GGSIPU defines PIO as a citizen of another country (not Pakistan or Bangladesh) who held an Indian passport or whose parent or grandparent was an Indian citizen; a foreign national is a non-Indian-origin citizen of another country.
GGSIPU international applicants need AIU equivalence for their qualification, a student visa and passport; the form asks for 12th aggregate, English pass, PCM and PCB percentages.

Maharashtra State CET Cell 2026 nursing brochure: NRI candidates are eligible only for up to 15% institute-quota seats in unaided private/minority colleges, and foreign nationals are not eligible for government or State-quota seats. This is the nursing brochure, not MBBS/BDS.

Maharashtra 2026 nursing brochure: OCI candidates are eligible for all seats only if OCI status was obtained before 4 March 2021, 10th and 12th were passed in Maharashtra and the candidate is domiciled or resident for 10 years.

Maharashtra 2026 nursing brochure: foreign HSC qualifications need UGC equivalence under the UGC (Recognition and Grant of Equivalence to Qualifications from Foreign Educational Institutions) Regulations 2025 dated 4 April 2025.

dasanit.org currently shows only DASA PG 2026; UG brochure is on csab.nic.in (cdnbbsr link). No 2027 brochure exists yet.
No SAT or other-board entrance rule exists in DASA UG; JEE Main 2026 is mandatory there.
Maharashtra MHT-CET exemption for NRI/OCI/PIO/CIWG/FN comes from a search summary of the MHT-CET 2026 brochure; not independently opened. NRI definition circular is 2025-26.

AIU: DASA brochure Annexure 2 reproduces the AIU list; aiu.ac.in pages seen only via search summary (IB needs 24 credits per AIU advisory 2016), not opened. Indian Gulf CBSE school rule not confirmed from AIU; DASA lists Gulf 12-year certificates as equivalent.
VIT 2027-28 page mixes 55% and 60% figures; seat share not stated.
BITS BITSAT figures read from the older BITSAT-2022 modality PDF; no 2027 cycle published.
MEA page does not mention the PIO-OCI merger.

Ask the counselling body, or the institution for NRI seats in private and deemed universities.
